title: Analytics: rollup tables/jobs for route experiment variant metrics
author: Mei Lin
release_notes: Adds experiment variant rollup datasets powering Console experiment results (latency/cost/error by {route, experiment_id, variant_id}).
description:
Context: Console Route Experiments results view needs stable, low-cardinality aggregations keyed by {route_id, experiment_id, variant_id} with common breakdowns (model_id, region) and a consistent time grain. We already emit experiment_id/variant_id in request context (ENG-9026), but the existing rollups only support {route_id, model_id, region} and do not handle experiment attribution drop or streaming retries cleanly.

What this PR does: (1) Introduces a dedicated rollup table family for experiment variant metrics at 5m and 1h grains. (2) Adds an incremental aggregation job (idempotent per time window) that consumes request-level OTel-derived facts and writes per-variant aggregates for latency, cost/token economics, throughput, and error rate. (3) Adds guardrail-oriented derived fields (p95/p99, error_rate, cost_per_1k_tokens) matching the Console MVP display + the Results API expectations. (4) Adds data quality checks to detect attribution gaps and pathological splits (e.g., variant has 0 traffic while experiment is “running”).

Schema details (new rollups): experiment_variant_metrics_5m and experiment_variant_metrics_1h keyed by: ts_bucket, account_id, route_id, experiment_id, variant_id, model_id, region. Metrics: request_count, success_count, error_count, error_rate, latency_ms_p50/p95/p99 (hdr-based rollup), ttft_ms_p50/p95, tokens_in_sum, tokens_out_sum, billed_tokens_sum, cost_usd_estimate_sum, cost_usd_per_1k_tokens, throughput_rps_avg, attribution_present_count, attribution_missing_count, attribution_drop_rate. Notes: We intentionally do NOT include stickiness_key / user_id / raw path to avoid cardinality blowups; route_id is the normalized route template (see route id normalization guidance) and aligns with ADR-048 attribution dimensions.

Aggregation job behavior: - Source: request_facts_v2 (populated from OTel spans + gateway logs) with experiment_id/variant_id fields. - Bucketing: time bucket is derived from request_end_ts; we treat retries as distinct requests but de-dup streaming “continuations” by request_id + attempt_id to avoid double-counting tokens and latency (this matches how the Console results interpret streaming retries). - Percentiles: Uses pre-aggregated HDR sketches stored in request_facts_v2; rollup merges sketches per bucket and exports p50/p95/p99 for fast query in Console. - Cost: cost_usd_estimate is computed using the existing per-model cost table (model_cost_profiles) and billed_tokens_sum; this keeps cost consistent with non-experiment route dashboards.

Data quality + safety: Adds checks in the rollup pipeline: (a) attribution_drop_rate > 2% emits a WARN log + metric (not a hard failure) to avoid blocking results during partial propagation; (b) ‘variant_0_traffic’ detector flags cases where an experiment is “running” but one or more variants have ~0 traffic for > 15m (often indicates assignment skew / missing sticky key / config propagation issues); (c) region+model sanity check to avoid silently dropping rows when model_id is missing (we bucket missing model_id as ‘unknown’ to keep totals consistent).

Performance considerations: - Adds partitions by day on ts_bucket and clustering by {account_id, route_id, experiment_id}. - Limits query dimensions to a small set that Console needs today; additional breakdowns (gpu_type, sdk_version, prompt_template_id) are explicitly out of scope due to cardinality/cost.

How this is used by Console: The Results API will query experiment_variant_metrics_5m for “last 6h / 24h” views and experiment_variant_metrics_1h for 7d+ windows. The API expects variant deltas to be computed server-side; this PR only provides the canonical aggregates.

Testing: - Unit tests for SQL compilation + schema validation. - Integration test in analytics pipeline harness that replays a small fixture dataset containing: 2 variants, mixed regions, streaming retry, and forced attribution-missing rows; asserts expected counts and percentiles.

Migration/rollout: - Safe additive tables. - Job is disabled by default behind the analytics feature flag ‘route_experiments_rollups’ until Console beta enablement. - Backfill is not included here; we’ll handle limited backfill once schema is stable (tracked separately).

Rollback: Disable the ‘route_experiments_rollups’ job; tables can remain without impacting existing dashboards.

References: ENG-9027, ENG-9026, ADR-048. Related support signal: SUP-24910 (stale results due to missing/late aggregates) — this PR adds explicit propagation/attribution visibility so we can distinguish data latency vs. UI cache issues.

conversation: Logan Wright (review): Can we confirm the dimensions match ADR-048 exactly? Specifically: do we want route_id normalized template or raw path? Raw path will explode cardinality if customers include IDs. Please add a short note in the PR + ensure we’re using the normalized route_id.

Mei Lin (author): Yep — route_id is the normalized template ID from the router, not the raw path. I added an explicit note under Schema details and a test case where raw paths differ but route_id is constant.

Caleb Johnson (review): Streaming retry de-dup looks good, but I’m worried about counting continuation spans as separate “requests” if attempt_id is missing. What happens when gateway doesn’t provide attempt_id?

Mei Lin (author): If attempt_id is missing we fall back to request_id only; that can undercount in the rare case of multiple true requests sharing request_id (should not happen) and overcount if continuations generate new request_id (should not happen). I added a metric `missing_attempt_id_count` so we can observe if this is happening in staging/beta.

Nadia Rahman (review): Cost calc: using billed_tokens_sum is correct. Please also include tokens_in/out sums for customers to understand prompt vs completion cost split; Console design wants to show this later.
Mei Lin (author): Added tokens_in_sum and tokens_out_sum to both rollups, and updated the README with an example query.

Allison Grant (review): Attribution drop rate check should not fail the job. Please ensure this is a WARN-only path; we can alert separately. Also consider a detector for “variant has 0 traffic” because that’s a common oncall symptom.
Mei Lin (author): Done — WARN-only for attribution_drop_rate, plus added `variant_0_traffic` detector output as a metric and a log line keyed by {account_id, route_id, experiment_id}.
Felix Schneider (review): Console will query by experiment_id and time range; can you cluster/index for that access pattern? The 5m table could get heavy for large tenants.
Mei Lin (author): Added clustering by {account_id, route_id, experiment_id} and documented the expected query patterns; also ensured the 5m table is TTL’d per our analytics retention defaults.
Logan Wright (final): Approved. This should unblock Results API work; please link the flag name in ENG-9027 so rollout sequencing is clear.
Mei Lin (author): Linked and added to the ticket. Merging.
